newsitem.title: USA: CSCE world sugar ends slightly firmer.
newsitem.headline: CSCE world sugar ends slightly firmer.

text.p: CSCE world sugar futures ended slightly higher Friday, in line with the London white sugar market, but trade was quiet ahead of the U.S. Labor Day holiday Monday which will shut New York markets.
CSCE October sugar ended up 0.05 cent at 11.78 cents, after trading in a narrow 11.74-11.80 cent range.
The focus was increasingly on the October/March roll, ahead of the October contract's expiry on September 30, traders said.
"But I think technically October sugar is forming a bull flag which projects to over 12.00 cents," one trader said.
Support is still seen around 11.50 cents, with resistance around 11.80 cents, basis October.
Tenders announced by both Syria and Egypt this week had provided some support, traders said, and there is still some uncertainty about the European beet crop.

Syria has tendered to buy 26,000 tonnes of whites and 26,000 tonnes of raws, for October/November delivery, while Egypt has two September tenders planned to buy 25,000 tonnes of whites or raws, followed by a tender for 25,000 tonnes of whites.

But longer term supplies are seen ample, with Cuban sugar planting reported to be 88 percent of the July-August plan or 104,250 acres, ahead of last year's 66 percent of plan. The government reported earlier it would sow 387,125 acres in July-December, up from 290,000 last year.
